reading.body:
The physical inputs to AI compute are now covered by insurance across the supply chain, and the one quantified lead time is grid equipment, with transformer and switchgear delays running to four years.

The ten coverages map to distinct failure points, from cargo shipments of high value accelerators to cleanroom contamination at packaging plants. This segmentation means insurers now treat AI hardware as a chain of specific physical risks rather than a single general property exposure. Foundry concentration in Taiwan and rare earth export bottlenecks are geopolitical risks, while thermal shock, cooling pump failures, and custom silicon logic flaws are operational risks inside the data center.

For AI scaling, the grid equipment lead time is the most direct constraint. Even if chips are fabricated and shipped, transformer and switchgear delays of up to four years can hold back new compute capacity. The data does not show premiums, loss history, or claim frequency, so it cannot say how expensive or how likely these failures are, only that coverage products exist for each one.
